title: The Deployments card on the opened goal: per environment, arm and confirm, refusals as words
description:
SPIDR child of task-84cd2e55aae942cf8d56657308215fde (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05), which measured at 11-12 files against a 10-file cap. dependsOn task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5 for the command kinds it dispatches.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS. The parent owns the card, the Needs-you roster, the Runs receipt row, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs. The Needs-you roster change alone forces three files (see the parent's plan), so the card and the surfaces cannot share one plan. This row is the CARD. The parent keeps Needs-you, Runs, the journey, the live drive and the docs.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: a Deployments card on the opened goal rendering, PER ENVIRONMENT, the target, the last deploy sha, time, url and status, with a Deploy arm/confirm; the port that spends the offer; and the card's own tests. NO Needs-you edit, NO Runs edit, NO Playwright journey, NO docs - all the parent's.

THE ONE SAFETY PROPERTY: PREVIEW AND PRODUCTION SIT ON THE SAME CARD, and the destructive one is a click away from the safe one. The confirm step must name the environment unmistakably, and a PRODUCTION deploy must show whether a release decision exists on the goal - so the operator sees what the deploy effect recorded rather than discovering it in a receipt afterwards.

- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-status-strip.tsx:33 carries a `publish: "cr-goal-publish"` entry - check whether a card on this screen is expected to join that map.
- THE TESTID NAMESPACE `cr.deploy` IS FREE: `git grep -c "cr\.deploy" -- apps tests` returned nothing. Confirm again before claiming it; `cr.board.*` was already taken once.
- goal-publish.test.tsx:204-215 asserts on its own SOURCE TEXT (readFileSync of goal-publish.tsx, then `not.toContain` for localStorage/sessionStorage and a retired key assembled rather than spelled so a repo-wide grep stays at zero). If this card holds no browser-local state either, copy that arm.</description>

definitionOfDone: The Deployments card renders PER ENVIRONMENT: target, last deploy sha, time, url and status. It dispatches the deploy kinds through offer-wire `spendOffer` via a port mirroring apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/publish-port.ts - no second decision wire, and no command dispatch inside the component.

THE CONFIRM STEP NAMES THE ENVIRONMENT UNMISTAKABLY. Assert, as its own arm, that a PRODUCTION confirm cannot be mistaken for a PREVIEW confirm: the rendered confirm text contains the environment name, and arming PREVIEW then confirming cannot dispatch PRODUCTION. This is the row's one safety property - an operator must not deploy production believing they clicked preview.

A PRODUCTION deploy SHOWS whether a release decision exists on the goal, in the confirm step, in both states - cited when one exists and stated plainly when none does. The operator sees it before deciding, not afterwards in a receipt.
The card is ABSENT - not a dead button - when the daemon offers no deploy. Assert absence by querying for the testid and finding nothing, not by asserting a disabled attribute.

All four refusal codes (DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED, DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE, DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT) render VERBATIM with operator words. DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING offers a way to set a target. DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carries the tool's last stderr line so a failure is diagnosable from the browser, not only from a receipt.

I re-measured at plan time and it returned NOTHING - the namespace is free. Re-check anyway; a peer may have claimed it since. (d) DECIDE WHERE THE CARD MOUNTS, and settle it by reading rather than assuming. `board-screen.tsx:17` (237 lines) and `goal-nodes.tsx:11` (97 lines) BOTH import `{ GoalPublish, publishOffer }`. Also check `goal-status-strip.tsx:33`, which carries a `publish: "cr-goal-publish"` entry - decide whether a Deployments card is expected to join that map, and state the decision either way rather than leaving it unconsidered. (e) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (f) `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/v2/` and note peer dirt; several goals/ files were dirty with another session's work earlier today, so read before editing and never revert.

THE PORT. NEW FILE `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/deploy-port.ts`, mirroring `publish-port.ts` - which is 29 lines and is the whole decision wire. Copy its SHAPE exactly: import `spendOffer` from "../approvals/offer-wire.js", declare the command kind and a `DEPLOY_LAYER` const, expose `createDeployPort(wire)` returning a frozen object whose `submit` calls `spendOffer(wire, KIND, affordance, payload, "ui-deploy", DEPLOY_LAYER)`. A SECOND DECISION WIRE IS A DESIGN REGRESSION (rail 2) - no fetch here, no dispatch inside any component. THE PAYLOAD IS WHERE THIS DIFFERS FROM PUBLISH AND IT MATTERS: publish carries `{goalId, remoteUrl}` for ONE target; deploy carries an ENVIRONMENT, and the environment is the safety-critical field. Take it as an explicit parameter, never defaulted and never inferred from component state - `submit(affordance, goalId, environment)`. Read publish-port.ts's docblock before writing yours: it explains why `remoteUrl` is ALWAYS SENT even when null (a missing key arrives as `undefined` and the daemon reads that as malformed, not as a default). Check task-04b3ce7e's delivered payload roster for the same trap and send every key the roster admits. Write the docblock in that file's voice, stating what the environment means and that nothing is deployed here - the daemon's effect runner performs the deploy and the receipt says what became of it.

THE CARD, AND THE ONE BUG THAT COPYING THE MODEL PRODUCES. NEW FILE `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-deployments.tsx` (goal-publish.tsx is 173 lines; stay at or under 250, rail 5). Mirror its structure: an offer-discovery export beside the component (`publishOffer` at :36-41 finds the offer by `commandKind` AND `targetAggregateId`), `useState` for armed/busy/answer, an `ActionButton` arm/confirm, a cancel button while armed, and an `aria-live` answer note. READ THIS BEFORE WRITING THE ARM. goal-publish.tsx:147 is `onClick={() => { if (!armed) { setArmed(true); return; } decide(); }}` with a BOOLEAN `armed`. That is safe for PUBLISH because there is exactly ONE target. THIS CARD HAS TWO ENVIRONMENTS ON THE SAME SURFACE, so a boolean `armed` shared across both rows is the row's safety property inverted: arm PREVIEW, then click PRODUCTION, and `armed` is already true - it dispatches PRODUCTION IMMEDIATELY, with no confirm, from one click on a button the operator has never confirmed. That is DoD-2's failure, and copying the model faithfully is exactly how you get it. ARM STATE MUST BE KEYED BY ENVIRONMENT: hold `armed: string | null` (the environment name), and on a click where `armed !== thisEnvironment` RE-ARM to this environment rather than confirming. Only a click where `armed === thisEnvironment` dispatches. THE CONFIRM LABEL NAMES THE ENVIRONMENT (DoD-2): publish's is `Confirm: push to ${remote}`; yours must carry the environment name itself, so the rendered text of a production confirm cannot read like a preview one. THE PRODUCTION RELEASE-DECISION LINE (DoD-3) IS PART OF THE CONFIRM, NOT A FOOTNOTE: when the environment is production, the confirm step states whether a release decision exists on the goal - cited when one does, stated plainly when none does. Both wordings are asserted in step 4, so write them as two explicit strings rather than a conditional fragment that renders empty. THE CARD IS ABSENT WHEN THERE IS NO OFFER (DoD-4): return null, never a disabled button - the test queries for the testid and expects nothing. NO BROWSER-LOCAL STATE: no localStorage, no sessionStorage (step 4 pins this by source text). ASCII-ONLY AND NO APOSTROPHE IN JSX TEXT (rail 5) - the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe, so write "the operator has not decided" and never "operator's decision"; check the diff for smart quotes and dashes pasted from a description.

THE TESTS, SAFETY ARM FIRST. NEW FILE `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-deployments.test.tsx`, modelled on goal-publish.test.tsx. (1) DoD-2, THE SAFETY ARM AND THE ROW'S MOST VALUABLE ARTIFACT, in two parts: (a) the rendered confirm text for PRODUCTION contains the environment name and is distinguishable from PREVIEW's; (b) ARM PREVIEW, THEN CLICK PRODUCTION, and assert NO dispatch occurred - the production button must move to armed, not fire. Assert on what the port RECEIVED (spy the port and check its calls), not on the button's label: a label can read correctly while the dispatch carries the other environment. This arm is what a boolean `armed` fails, and it must be written so that it does fail against one. (2) DoD-3: a production confirm with a release decision present CITES it; with none it states so plainly. Both wordings, both asserted - a conditional that renders empty passes an "is present" check while telling the operator nothing. (3) DoD-4: with no deploy offer on the frame, `screen.queryByTestId("cr.deploy.root")` is NULL - absence by query, never a disabled attribute (goal-publish.test.tsx:200 is the exact precedent, `queryByTestId(...).toBeNull()`). (4) DoD-5: all four refusal codes render VERBATIM with operator words - DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING additionally offers a way to set a target, and DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carries the tool's last stderr line, asserted with a distinctive planted string so a generic message cannot pass. (5) DoD-1: the card renders target, sha, time, url and status PER ENVIRONMENT - assert with two environments present that each row carries its own values and they are not crossed. (6) THE SOURCE-TEXT ARM, copied from goal-publish.test.tsx:204-215: readFileSync the component and assert `not.toContain` for localStorage and sessionStorage. Note the idiom in that file - a retired key is ASSEMBLED (`["moe","publish","remoteUrl"].join(".")`) rather than spelled, so a repo-wide grep for it stays at zero; if you pin any string that way, use the same trick and say why in a comment.

MOUNT IT, DRILL IT, GATE IT. (a) MOUNT the card on the opened-goal surface chosen in step 1(d), following how `GoalPublish` is composed there (board-screen.tsx:17 or goal-nodes.tsx:11), and pass it the offer discovered by the export from step 3. (ii) Make the production release-decision line render empty when no decision exists and confirm the DoD-3 "states plainly" arm reds - an absent line and a line saying "no release decision" are different facts to an operator. THE MODEL THIS ROW IS TOLD TO COPY IS UNSAFE WHEN COPIED. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 3 new files plus one composition line.

Rail 2 says reuse the publish card's arm/confirm shape, and that is right — but following it faithfully produces exactly the bug DoD-2 exists to prevent.

## The failure, concretely

`goal-publish.tsx:147`:

```js
onClick={(): void => { if (!armed) { setArmed(true); return; } decide(); }}
```

`armed` is a **boolean**. That is safe for publish, which has exactly **one** target. This card has **two environments on one surface**, so a shared boolean means:

> arm PREVIEW → click PRODUCTION → `armed` is already `true` → **production dispatches immediately**, from a single click on a button the operator never confirmed.

That is DoD-2's failure reached by doing what the row asks. The fix is small: hold `armed: string | null` keyed by environment, and a click where `armed !== thisEnvironment` **re-arms** rather than confirming. Drill (i) reproduces the boolean and requires the safety arm to go red against it — a safety arm that has never failed is not evidence.

Rejected a per-environment boolean pair: it lets two rows be armed at once, which is a second confusing state on a card whose entire point is that the operator knows which environment they are about to touch. One `armed: string | null` makes "exactly one environment is armed" true by construction.

## Two ways the safety arm could pass while the bug ships

- **Asserting the button label.** A label can read "Confirm: deploy to production" while the dispatch carries preview. The arm must assert on **what the port received** — which is also why the plan makes `environment` an explicit port parameter rather than read from component state at dispatch time, so the confirmed value and the dispatched value cannot diverge.
- **DoD-3's two wordings are two facts.** A conditional that renders *empty* when no release decision exists passes an "is it present" check while telling the operator nothing. Both strings explicit, both asserted; drill (ii) proves the empty case reds.

## Carried over from the model, worth keeping

`publish-port.ts`'s docblock records that `remoteUrl` is **always sent even as null**, because a missing key arrives as `undefined` and the daemon reads that as malformed rather than as a default. Check task-04b3ce7e's delivered payload roster for the same behaviour before assuming an omitted key is safe.

`publishOffer` matches on **both** `commandKind` and `targetAggregateId` — matching on kind alone would pick up another goal's offer.

## Measurements

- `cr.deploy` namespace: **free** at plan time (`git grep -c` returned nothing). Re-check anyway; the row asks because `cr.board.*` was taken once.
- **board-screen.tsx is 237 lines against a 250 target** — about 13 lines of headroom. The mount is a composition line; if it needs more than that, the wiring belongs in the card.
- Two candidate mount sites both import `GoalPublish` (board-screen.tsx:17, goal-nodes.tsx:11). The plan makes the worker decide which is the opened goal and **say how they can tell**, rather than guessing.

Noted your correction comment about the corrupt description tail — step 1 opens with it so a worker does not read `placeholder` as unspecified scope.
